title: What makes an AI agent different?
description: Understand AI agents, tool access, permissions, and the importance of review checkpoints.

sections.title: From answering to taking actions
sections.body: A chatbot usually responds to a conversation. An agent can use tools and take several steps toward a goal, such as finding a document and preparing an update. Products use the word agent in different ways, so inspect the actual capabilities. A workflow with fixed rules may be ordinary automation even when an AI model handles one step.
bullets: Ask which tools the system can use.
Find out whether it can read, create, change, send, or delete information.

sections.title: Keep permissions proportional to the task
sections.body: Give an agent only the access needed for its job. Reading a public page is different from sending an email or changing a customer record. Set review checkpoints before actions that create commitments, expose information, or are hard to undo. Keep a record of what the agent did so you can investigate mistakes.
bullets: Start with read-only access and a small scope.
Require confirmation for consequential external actions.

sections.title: Test failures before relying on the workflow
sections.body: Agents can misread instructions, use a tool incorrectly, or follow malicious instructions hidden in retrieved content. Test missing files, conflicting information, unexpected responses, and permission errors. Decide how the workflow should stop and alert a person. A successful demonstration is a starting point, not evidence that every situation is handled.
bullets: Use a test environment and synthetic data.
Check time limits, spending limits, and recovery steps.

example.title: A sensible review checkpoint
example.text: An assistant may prepare a draft reply from an approved policy. A person checks the facts and recipient before sending. The task benefits from automation while the external commitment remains visible.

exercise: Sketch a three-step agent workflow. Mark the information it reads, the actions it can take, and where a person should review the result.

faq.question: Are agents fully autonomous?
faq.answer: Some can operate for multiple steps, but autonomy depends on the product and configuration. Important actions still need suitable controls and accountability.

faq.question: Is WebMCP an AI agent?
faq.answer: No. WebMCP is an evolving browser interface that lets a website expose defined tools to compatible agents.

sources.name: OWASP: Top risks for generative AI applications
